text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein, in speech to army officers, says Jordan stands firm in the face of threats and dangers. "We did not surrender...There is no alternative to peace but war and destruction."
- No success in merger talks between Bank of Jordan and Jordan-Kuwait Bank. Jordan-Kuwait board opposes merger.
- Dustour poll finds opinion divided about whether upcoming elections should have international monitors.
- Parliamentary speaker Saed Hayel Srour says Jordan would never participate in an alliance which harmed Arab interests.
- 2,700 Austrian tourists switched holidays last month from Jordan to Israel because of poor tourist services in Jordan.
- Changes expected to retirement law soon which aim both to raise efficiency, save government money, and ensure that people are still covered by social security.
- "This country is not the substitute homeland for Palestinians or others," King Hussein tells army chiefs.
